answer: The AI Act requires that there be a sufficiently detailed summary on the use of copyright-protected training data. Providers must disclose the use of copyrighted material in the training data, which poses a significant burden due to the lack of uniformity in copyright law across the EU. This requirement aims to enable authors and other rights holders to assess whether their rights have been infringed. However, it is noted that there is currently no effective way to detect when AI-generated content may be related to existing copyrighted content, nor is it clear who owns the intellectual property of the outputs generated by generative models.
